name: Magic-Tap
summary: A virtual-hand selection technique that triggers from finger kinematics: when the fingertip enters a target, a characteristic deceleration pattern signals a deliberate tap, so no dwell or pinch is needed.
howItWorks: While the fingertip is inside a target, speed and acceleration thresholds tuned in a first study separate intentional taps from passing through; a pre-trigger state and switch logic prevent accidental selections. In a second study (Meta Quest), Magic-Tap was compared with Touch, Dwell-Time and Pinch: its completion time was comparable to Touch while keeping a significantly lower error rate.
advantages: As fast as touch with fewer accidental selections.
limitations: Thresholds must be tuned per user or setting.

relationships.note: Adds kinematic intent detection to touch-based virtual-hand selection.
Compared with Touch, Dwell-Time and Pinch variants.
